children: AMZN Q3: revenue $201.94B, EPS $1.89 (slightly below). AWS revenue ~$46B (+39%), AWS operating income ~$17.8B. TTM free cash flow -$42.4B. Qtr capex ~$76B; 2026 capex ~ $220B. Shares fell premarket.
Amazon (AMZN) secured a supplier financing line up to $80 billion to fund AI infrastructure, effective early 2027 through Q3 2028; lenders will have collateral rights on assets bought with the funds.
Amazon (AMZN) long-term debt surged from $65.6B year-end 2025 to $173.1B on Sept 30, 2026, more than doubling as company raised funds mainly for AWS AI data center investments.
AMZN five-year CDS hit a record 94 bps after weak quarterly results, higher-than-expected capex and slowest e‑commerce growth in three years; move coincided with tech peers' record CDS levels.
Amazon (AMZN): AWS says AI inference now makes up over half of its AI revenue. Chip-related revenue is rising double- to triple-digit as Graviton and Trainium deployments increase.
Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) shares fell about 6.7% in premarket trading after the company’s earnings release, with market reaction attributed in the summary to concerns about a rising debt load.
Amazon (AMZN) results raised trader focus on whether big tech’s heavy AI infrastructure spending will generate sustainable profits, amid broader market scrutiny of returns on such investments.
Bank of America notes Amazon (AMZN) investment-grade bonds yield about 6.8%–7.4% as hyperscalers fund heavy AI capex, grouping AMZN with higher-yielding IG peers tied to AI spending.
Amazon reported Q3 2026 interest expense of $1.69B versus $538M year-ago; interest income $1.19B. After tax net interest impact ~ $820M, or ~$0.075 per share.
Amazon (AMZN) said in its Q3 call Bedrock now supports China’s Kimi and GLM open models; CEO Andy Jassy said Bedrock mixes proprietary and open models and aims to scale toward AWS EC2 levels.
